title: Cross sterility is incidental on reproductive differences, not specially endowed

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Cross sterility is incidental on reproductive differences, not specially endowed

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The sterility of first crosses and of hybrids is not a quality specially endowed to keep species distinct but is incidental on unknown differences, chiefly in the reproductive systems, of the species crossed.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The foregoing rules and facts, on the other hand, appear to me clearly to indicate that the sterility both of first crosses and of hybrids is simply incidental or dependent on unknown differences, chiefly in the reproductive systems, of the species which are crossed.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter VIII, “Hybridism”; section “Sterility not a special endowment, but incidental on other differences”. Scope: all species capable of being crossed

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch08-08: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.50

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Mechanisms of incompatibility and signatures of reinforcement are empirically testable. The teleological contrast 'specially endowed' has no unique modern measurement, limiting discrimination.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Test whether hybrid sterility is mechanistically explained by mapped reproductive incompatibilities and whether those variants show evidence of selection specifically to prevent gene flow. Incidental pleiotropic incompatibilities support the claim; consistent barrier-specific adaptation opposes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Absence of historical purpose is not directly measurable.

Reinforcement can specially strengthen barriers after incidental incompatibilities arise.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The anti-teleological claim can be turned into a geographic prediction, and an open fly dataset already contains isolation, distance, and overlap. That is informative but not decisive, because incidental divergence and several selection scenarios can produce the same distance relationship. The vague residue, unknown differences chiefly in the reproductive system, is not an additional dataset test.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare postzygotic sterility in sympatric and allopatric pairs after accounting for genetic distance. Sterility that tracks divergence in allopatry, where it could not have been endowed to prevent crossing, supports an incidental byproduct; sterility concentrated only where species meet, beyond what distance predicts, would favor a special isolating endowment.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Unknown differences in the reproductive system' is not itself a measured variable.

Range-overlap scores in the fly table do not extend to the full scope of crossable species.

The rival hypothesis of reinforcement applies more clearly to premating barriers than to sterility.
